GÍR.NI: knife (?), a cutting tool: written with the two signs GÍR and NI, which I leave unread; “knife” is the sense the law needs, the exact kind of tool I cannot say, UNCERTAIN: ina GÍR.NI siparrim “with a bronze knife” · Sumerogram, reading uncertain
siparrum: bronze (written with the Sumerogram UD.KA.BAR, the three signs UD, KA and BAR, with no ending written): siparrim (genitive) “of bronze”; the case ending is the grammar’s, not written · noun, Sumerogram
nagabtum: UNCERTAIN: a word I cannot read (Harper’s na-gab-ti); the context suggests a part of or near the eye, but the meaning is not secure, and neither is the exact form: nagabti (na-gab-ti, before a genitive: “the nagabtu of …”), nagabtašu (na-gab-ta-šu) “his nagabtu”, with -šu · noun, sense uncertain
mâtum-Š: Š-stem (causative) of mâtum “to die”: to make die, to kill: uštamīt (uš-ta-mi-it, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has caused (him) to die” · Š-stem verb
šebirtum: break, fracture (Harper’s sense; from šebērum “to break”): šebirtam (še-bi-ir-tam, accusative) “a broken (part)”, said of a bone · noun
šalāmum-Š: Š-stem (causative) of šalāmum “to be whole, sound”: to make whole, to heal: uštalim (uš-ta-li-im, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has made (it) whole”, said of a broken bone · Š-stem verb
šerʾānum: UNCERTAIN: a body part, perhaps “sinew, muscle”, a guess from the sound and from the sense (something that can be sick and be healed): šerʾānam (še-ir-ḫa-nam, the ʾ written with the sign ḪA, accusative) “a sinew (?)”; Harper prints the spelling as two words, še-ir ḫa-nam · noun, sense uncertain
marṣum: sick, ill: marṣam (mar-ṣa-am, accusative) “sick”, agreeing with its noun · adjective
3: three — three wedges: šalāš “three” (šalāš šiqil kaspim “three shekels of silver”); the spoken form is reconstructed from the numeral · numeral
gallābum: barber (written with the Sumerogram ŠU.I, the two signs ŠU and I, with no ending written; from galābum “to shave”): gallābum (nominative), gallābim (genitive), gallābam (accusative); the endings are the grammar’s, not written · noun, Sumerogram
šû: UNCERTAIN: lā šēm (la še-e-im, the signs ŠE, E and IM) in “a slave not his”, read as a form of the pronoun šû “he, his”, from the context and not from the form: wardi lā šēm “of a slave who is not his” · pronoun, form uncertain
idāṣ: UNCERTAIN: a verb I cannot read (the sign AZ read aṣ); the lemma is only the form idāṣ, and “to deceive” is the sense the law seems to need, not something the form shows: idāṣma (i-da-aṣ-ma, with -ma) “he has deceived (?), and” · verb, sense uncertain
bābum: gate, door: bābīšu (KÁ-šu, the gate sign KÁ and ŠU, with -šu “his”) “his gate”: ina bābīšu “at his gate”; the ending is the grammar’s, KÁ being a Sumerogram · noun
kalālum-Š: Š-stem (causative) of kalālum “to be complete”: to complete, finish: ušaklilšum (u-ša-ak-li-il-šum, with -šum “for him”) “he has completed (it) for him”, said of a house · Š-stem verb
SAR: SAR, a unit of area (the plot a house stands on), written with the one sign SAR and left unread: ana ištēn SAR bītim “for one SAR of house” · Sumerogram, reading not given
šipru: work, task, workmanship: šipiršu (ši-bi-ir-šu, the sign BI for pi, with -šu “his”) “his work”: šipiršu lā udanninma “he has not made his work strong” · noun
maqātum: to fall, collapse: imqutma (im-ku-ut-ma, preterite + -ma) “it has fallen, and” · imqutu (im-ku-tu, imqut with the subjunctive -u) “(which) fell”, “and it fell”: bītam imqutu “the house that fell” · verb
uštēṣbi: UNCERTAIN: a Š-stem perfect of a root I do not know; “to make right, true” is only a guess from the context: uštēṣbima (uš-te-iṣ-bi-ma, with -ma) “he has made (it) right (?), and”; the lemma is only the form · Š-stem verb, sense uncertain
igārum: wall (written with the Sumerogram É.GAR₈, É and a second sign keyed GAR₃, the nearest sign in the sign glossary, so the key is UNCERTAIN; no ending written): igārum (nominative), igāram (accusative) “wall”; the endings are the grammar’s · noun, Sumerogram
qatāpum: UNCERTAIN: iqtup (iq-tu-up) has the shape of a preterite of qatāpum; “has given way” (of a wall) is only the sense the context seems to need, not something the form shows · verb, sense uncertain
malaḫum: boatman, sailor (written with the Sumerogram MÁ.DU.DU, the signs MÁ, DU and DU, i.e. MÁ.LAḪ₄; no ending written): malaḫum (nominative), malaḫim (genitive), malaḫam (accusative); the endings are the grammar’s · noun, Sumerogram
elippum: boat, ship (feminine; written with the Sumerogram GIŠ.MÁ, the two signs GIŠ and MÁ, with no ending written): elippum (nominative), elippam (accusative), elippim (genitive), elippi “boat of” (construct, before a genitive); elippišu (GIŠ.MÁ-šu) “his boat”, and elippušu (GIŠ.MÁ-šu, Harper’s elippu-šu) “his boat” as the subject of tebiat; the endings are the grammar’s · noun, Sumerogram
ipḫi: UNCERTAIN: a verb I cannot read; “to caulk” (make watertight) is not shown by the form, only the sense a boatman’s fee for work on a boat seems to need; the lemma is only the form: ipḫi (ip-ḫi), ipḫima (ip-ḫi-ma, with -ma) “he has caulked (?)” · verb, sense uncertain
takālum-D: UNCERTAIN: the D-stem of takālum “to trust”, taken as “to make trustworthy, reliable” from the meaning of the stem, not from the context: utakkilma (u-tak-ki-il-ma, with -ma): lā utakkilma “he has not made (it) reliable (?), and” · D-stem verb, sense uncertain
izzapar: UNCERTAIN: a verb I cannot read; it has the shape of an N-stem preterite (a present would be izzappar), but the root is not known; “is spoilt” is only the sense the next clause seems to need: izzapar (iz-za-par) · verb, sense uncertain
naqārum: UNCERTAIN: to tear down, demolish, from the sense of the clause: inaqqarma (i-na-qar-ma, the sign GAR read qar; present + -ma) “he shall tear down, and” · verb, sense uncertain
tebûm-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem of tebûm, here “to sink” (transitive: to sink a boat), a sense taken from the stem and the law, not shown by the form; the opposite of uštēliašši “he has raised her” (see elûm-Š): uttebbi (ut-te-bi, ut-te-ib-bi, perfect) “he has sunk (it)”; utebbima (u-te-ib-bi-ma, preterite + -ma) “he sank, and”; utebbû (u-te-ib-bu-u, with the subjunctive -u) “(which) he sank”: elippam ša utebbû “the boat that he sank” · D-stem verb, sense uncertain
suluppum: dates (written with the Sumerogram ZÚ.LUM, the signs KA and LUM): suluppam (accusative); the ending is the grammar’s, not written · noun, Sumerogram
ṣīnum: UNCERTAIN: a word I cannot read with certainty (ṣi-nim, genitive), in the phrase mimma šumšu ša ṣīnim “anything whatever of ṣīnum”, after the goods loaded on a boat; “cargo” is only the sense the context suggests · noun, sense uncertain
iṣēn: UNCERTAIN: a verb I cannot read; “to load” (a boat) is only the context’s sense, not shown by the form; the lemma is only the form: iṣēnši (i-ṣi-en-ši, with -ši “her”, the boat) “he has loaded her (?)” · verb, sense uncertain
elûm-Š: Š-stem (causative) of elûm “to go up”: to raise, make go up: uštēliašši (uš-te-li-a-aš-ši, with -ši “her”, the boat) “he has raised her”, said of a boat that was sunk · Š-stem verb
maḫirtum: UNCERTAIN: a kind of boat, sense unknown: maḫirtim (ma-ḫi-ir-tim, genitive; Harper restores part of the word in §240): ša maḫirtim “the one of the maḫirtu”, elippum ša maḫirtim “a boat of the maḫirtu” · noun, sense uncertain
mukkelbītum: UNCERTAIN: a kind of boat, sense unknown: mukkelbītim (mu-uk-ki-el-bi-tim, genitive; Harper restores parts of the word in §240): elippam ša mukkelbītim “a boat of the mukkelbītu” · noun, sense uncertain

__broaden__.tebûm: to rise; Š-stem: ušetbûšuma “they shall make him rise (be removed)” · stative tebiat (te-bi-a-at) “is sunk”, said of a boat: elippišu tebiat “his boat is sunk”; here the sense is “sink”, not “rise”, and it is taken from the law, UNCERTAIN; the D-stem “to sink” (transitive) is entered as tebûm-D
__broaden__.abbuttum: UNCERTAIN: Harper “service, slavery”; later dictionaries read a mark of slavery: abbuttam (ab-bu-ut-tam, accusative), used with šakānum “to set, impose” (abbuttam išakkan); the sense is not secure · abbutti (ab-bu-ti, the construct before wardi, “the abbuttum of …”), what a barber shaves off a slave who is not his: abbutti wardi lā šēm ugallib “he has shaved off the abbuttum of a slave not his”; as before “slave-mark” is the later dictionaries’ sense, and that it was a hair-style is not in the text: UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.epēšum: to do, make: epēšim “doing” · to work (land): ippeš(ma) (present): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field” · to build (?) (a house): bītam ippēšma(?) “he builds a house, and”, the verb broken; iteppuš (?) in a broken line · ippešū (i-ib-bi-šu) “they shall do (work), they shall work” (present plural) · īpušu (i-pu-šu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(which) he built”: to make, build (a house) · ipuš (i-pu-uš, the sign BU read pu) “he made”: bīssu ipuš “he made his house”, i.e. set up a house of his own (preterite) · īpušma (i-bu-uš-ma, the sign BU read pu; preterite + -ma) “he made, and”: ṣimmam kabtam īpušma “he has made a severe wound”; bītam īpušma “he has built a house, and” · ippeš (i-ib-bi-eš, ibbi for ippi; present) “he shall rebuild”: bītam imqutu ippeš “he shall rebuild the house that fell”
__broaden__.balāṭum-D: to let live, keep alive (D-stem, factitive of balāṭum “to live”): uballaṭ “he lets (her) live” · ubtalliṭ (ub-tal-li-iṭ, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has healed”, the D-stem making “live” into “make live”: awīlam ubtalliṭ “he has healed the man”
__broaden__.petûm: to open; of land, to bring into cultivation: iptete “he has opened” · preterite ipte, iptēma “he opened” · iptēma (ip-te-ma) “he has opened, and”, of a part of the body, with a knife
__broaden__.kabtum: heavy; grave (of an offence): arnam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a heavy offence” · of a wound, severe: ṣimmam kabtam (kab-tam, accusative) “a severe wound”
__broaden__.galābum-D: to shave (D-stem): ugallabū “they shall shave” · ugallib (u-gal-li-ib) “he has shaved off” and ugdallib (ug-da-al-li-ib, perfect) “he has shaved off”, of a barber and a slave-mark; ugallibu (u-gal-li-bu, first person with the subjunctive -u, in a quoted oath) “I shaved”: lā ugallibu “I did not shave”
__broaden__.bānûm: creator; bānîšu “his creator” · builder (ŠITIM): bānûm “the builder”, bānîm šuāti “of that builder”, one who builds a house; the sign Harper numbers 168 is keyed ŠITIM tentatively, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.idum: hire, wages (Harper: ID, the ideogram for hire): idi našpakim “the hire of the bin”, written with the single sign Á (A₂, “arm; hire”); the case ending is not written, so idi (construct, before a genitive) is an assumed reading, UNCERTAIN · idīšu (Á-šu, with -šu “his”) “his fee”, the physician’s pay: ana asîm idīšu “to the physician as his fee”; the case vowel is UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.šuššum: one-sixth (written IGI.6.GAL, “the sixth part”): šuššum “a sixth”; in the silver rate it is followed by 6 še, “one-sixth and 6 grains” (IGI.6.GAL šeššet šeʾam) · šuššat (IGI.6.GAL, before kaspim) “one sixth”, of a shekel of silver; the unit is not written, and the spoken form is reconstructed, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.rebûm: fourth: rebûtim šattim “in the fourth year” · rebūt (IGI.4.GAL) “one quarter”: rebūt šīmišu “a quarter of its price”; the spoken form is reconstructed, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.mišlum: half: ana mišlāni “for halves” (in halves) · mišil (mi-ši-il) “half of”, before a noun: mišil šīmišu “half his price”, mišil šīmiša “half her price”
__broaden__.šīmum: purchase, purchase price · šīmišu (ŠÁM-šu, with -šu “his”) “his price”, of a slave: mišil šīmišu “half of his price” · šīmiša (ŠÁM-ša, with -ša “her”) “her price”, of a boat: mišil šīmiša “half her price”; šīmišu “its price”, of an animal: rebūt šīmišu “a quarter of its price”
__broaden__.ḫalālum: to hang up: iḫallalūšu “they shall hang him” (in the breach he cut) · iḫallalūšu (i-ḫa-al-la-lu-šu) “they shall hang him”, at his gate: ina bābīšu iḫallalūšu; “hang” is the usual sense of the verb, not shown by the form, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.danānum-D: D-stem of danānum “to be strong”: to strengthen, make firm (a dike): dunnunim (infinitive) “to strengthen”, udanninma (preterite, with -ma) “he strengthened, and …” · udannan (u-dan-na-an, present) “he shall make strong”, of a wall, and udannanma (with -ma), of a boat: igāram udannan “he shall make the wall strong”; lā udanninma (preterite + -ma) “he has not made (his work) strong”, udanninuma (with the subjunctive -u before -ma)
__broaden__.ḫalāqum-D: D-stem of ḫalāqum “to be lost, to perish”: to destroy, cause to be lost: uḫalliqu (preterite, with the relative -u) “(the grain) he destroyed” · uḫtalliq (uḫ-ta-al-li-iq, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has destroyed”: šumma makkūr uḫtalliq “if he has destroyed property”; of a boatman, ù lū uḫtalliq “or has destroyed (it)”
__broaden__.egûm: to be careless, neglect (Harper: “to be careless”): itēgi(ma) “he has been negligent, and” · igûma (i-gu-ma) “(who) was careless, and” (the preterite igi with the relative -u, as ilqû beside ilqe, then -ma) · īgīma (i-gi-ma, preterite + -ma) “he was careless, and”: malaḫum īgīma “the boatman was careless, and”
